newsitem.title: UK: BAT gains after rise in Philip Morris.
newsitem.headline: BAT gains after rise in Philip Morris.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T. Industries Plc rose in heavy trading on Tuesday amid continued restructuring talk and following a sharp overnight jump in U.S. tobacco group Philip Morris Cos, traders said.
B.A.T stock was up 10-1/2 pence, or 2.2 percent, at 487 by 1242 GMT, after earlier touching a four-month high of 489p.
Trading volume reached 12.7 million shares, making it the most active stock in the UK market.
"Philip Morris were up quite a lot last night, there's a very good market and plenty of buyers for this one (BAT)," one market maker said.
Philip Morris rallied $4-3/4 to 114-1/4 on Wall Street after Goldman Sachs raised its 12-month price target to $135 from $125.
Goldman analyst Marc Cohen said part of the reason for the revision was that legal pressure on tobaco companies in the U.S. would ease next year.

One UK trader said B.A.T had been reappraised in recent sessions amid continuing talk that the company will seek a merger partner for its insurance operations, possibly as a prelude to a demerger of its tobacco and financial services arms.
"BAT stock had looked oversold on the threat of US tobacco lawsuits and there has been talk of a financial services deal," the trader said.
"The stock was too cheap, it has been re-rated, people have been looking around for value in this market."
B.A.T said yesterday it had an "open mind" about a demerger.
